reported.title: ADC accumulator overflows int, producing wildly wrong percent
reported.description: `sum` is declared `int` (line 11) and accumulates up to WINDOW=50 raw samples (lines 54-55) before dividing at line 59. With 10-bit readings up to 1023, the sum reaches ~51150, exceeding the signed 16-bit int maximum of 32767 and wrapping negative, so `avg` and the resulting percent go badly negative. Measured evidence: printed -297.7 % and -140.3 % at full-scale inputs, off by 647.7 % and 640.3 %. Firmware printed -297.7 % at 4.00 s while the injected input was 350.0 to 350.0 %: off by 647.7 % (tolerance ±3). 7 of 7 values were wrong.

reported.title: Blocking button handling and delay stretch the pct: period
reported.description: The loop always waits IDLE_MS=20 ms (line 79) and additionally blocks 30 ms per detected LOW on D5 (lines 65-69), and the pct print only occurs when the 50-sample window fills (lines 57-63) rather than on a fixed 1000 ms cadence. Repeated or bouncing presses add cumulative delay, so the interval between `pct:` lines drifts well past the ±150 ms tolerance. Measured evidence: worst gaps of 1246 ms, 1337 ms and 1733 ms. Expected /^pct: / every 1000 ± 150 ms; 4 of 7 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 1246 ms.

judge_input.spec:
- Concentration probe on A4 at 10 mV per percent; force-sample button on D5 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Average a rolling window of ADC samples and print `pct: <value>` about once per second.
- Printed percent must stay within ±3.0 of the injected probe value.
- Lines matching `pct: ` must appear every 1000 ms ±150 ms.
- Holding D5 LOW may emit a `blend force last=<n>` note without replacing the periodic `pct:` stream.
- Every 1000 ms also print `blend batches=<n>` for batch accounting.
